title: A credit memo's due date on a statement counts on the location's calendar
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: A Net 30 customer at a location with daylight saving time has a credit memo, and you check its statement.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds Net 30 at {Location-A}, whose time zone has daylight saving time, and has a credit memo {Credit-memo-A} dated Oct 20, 2026.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S11-12 Customer, {Location-A} is in Edmonton and {Credit-memo-A} is CM-3576.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open {Customer-A}'s statement.
  2. Open the customer's unpaid transactions list.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the credit memo's due date reads Nov 19, 2026 (Oct 20 + 30 days; the Nov 1 clock change does not move it). Before the release this screen could show one day less; the later date is the correct one.
  • Step 2: the credit memo's due date reads Nov 19, 2026, the same.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates), story SV-11680 (Story 11, Release day: what changes for existing users)

  • S11-R14: “Screens that recalculate a due date from the term rather than showing a stored due date (the A/R dashboard for records with no stored due date, and credit memo due dates on statements and the unpaid transactions list) can show a date one day later than they showed before release, for a term whose span crosses a daylight-saving change. The later date is the correct one; it is the same fix as SV-11414. Stored due dates are never rewritten. The Vendor Bill Export, which today recalculates from the vendor's current term, shows each vendor invoice's stored due date from release (S7-R11), so after a vendor's term changes it still matches the vendor invoice.”
  • S7-E2: “Due dates already stored on existing invoices and vendor invoices are never rewritten. A screen that recalculates a due date from the customer's term shows the date on the calendar of the transaction's own location (S7-R6, S11-R14).”
  • Out of Scope: “Statements, the customer portal and A/R aging gain no new screens and show no credit term name on their own screens (an invoice document opened from the portal prints the term as any printed invoice does); see S11-R14 for the due dates they recalculate. They show stored due dates, except where one is recalculated today: the A/R dashboard for records with no stored due date, and credit memo due dates on statements and the unpaid transactions list. Those recalculated dates are counted on the calendar of the record's own location (S7-R6).”
  • S7-R6: “Due dates are counted on the calendar of the location the invoice or vendor invoice belongs to, never the location of the user, API connection or import that creates or views it, so a daylight saving change inside the span never moves the date: an Edmonton invoice dated Oct 5 on "10th of the following month" is due Nov 10 (not Nov 9).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
